title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 15 (Alteration of Memorandum or Articles to Be Noted in Every Copy)

content.overview: Section 15 requires that every copy of the memorandum or articles issued after an alteration must include the alteration. Issuing a copy that does not embody the alteration is an offence punishable with fine.
content.glance: State the duty to note alterations in every copy of the memorandum or articles issued after the alteration; note the penalty for default.
content.study: Where an alteration is made in the memorandum or articles, every copy of the memorandum or articles issued after the date of the alteration must be in accordance with the alteration. A company that issues a copy which is not so in accordance is liable to a fine. The provision ensures that members and third parties who receive copies of the constitutional documents see the current text. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in s. 15 and link to the alteration powers under ss. 13 and 14.

sections.heading: Duty to Embody Alterations
sections.body: Every copy of the memorandum or articles issued after an alteration must include that alteration.

sections.heading: Penalty
sections.body: Issuing a non-updated copy attracts a fine as prescribed.

provisions.title: Alteration of memorandum or articles to be noted in every copy

examples.title: Updated copy issued
examples.body: After an objects alteration under s. 13, the company issues only copies that include the new objects. Section 15 is complied with.

examples.title: Stale copy issued
examples.body: The company issues a copy of the articles that omits a recent special-resolution alteration. Section 15 is breached and a fine may follow.

hypotheticals.question: Must old copies held by members be recalled?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 15 regulates copies issued after the alteration; it does not by itself require recall of every prior copy, but new issues must be current.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 15 apply to both memorandum and articles?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. It covers every copy of the memorandum or articles issued after the alteration.

distinctions.title: s. 15 (noting alterations) vs ss. 13–14 (power to alter)
distinctions.right: Power and procedure to make the alteration

misconceptions.trap: Alteration is complete once the special resolution is passed; copies need not be updated.
misconceptions.correction: Section 15 requires every subsequently issued copy to embody the alteration.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 15 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the alteration and its date. II. Check whether copies issued after that date embody the alteration. III. State the penalty if not. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Alteration date; copies issued; whether updated; penalty exposure; precise relief.
